answer: A market can resist fake identities by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake before it trades, like an ember that only burns while the agent behaves. A reputation registry ties the stake to verified work, and when an agent cheats the stake is slashed, so one operator spinning up a plume of fake accounts must fund every one and lose each bond when caught. The cost grows with each identity, so at dawn of a new epoch a Sybil farm faces real losses rather than free names, making one honest identity the cheaper path.
